signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Strait of Hormuz Risk
signals.text: CHF/JPY trades at 127.35 (implied) as JPY outperforms G10 peers by +1.230% while CHF lags by -0.789%, creating a significant 2.019% performance spread. The pair faces a carry disadvantage of -100bp (SNB 0.0% vs BoJ 1.0%), yet JPY remains bid following Tier-1 geopolitical headlines regarding shipping route disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the low VIX at 14.9, the specific commodity-linked supply risk is driving JPY outperformance ahead of the BoJ Summary of Opinions. JPY ESI at +17.8 confirms the currency is supported by a sustained run of data beats relative to expectations. Trade bias: Bearish CHF/JPY; JPY outperformance theme persists on geopolitical friction. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions release Monday. Risk: Oman-mediated shipping deal resolves Hormuz tension, removing the JPY-specific risk bid.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Complacency + Technical Breakdown
signals.text: USD/JPY at 157.84 has collapsed through its SMA20/50/200 cluster (161.24, 161.17, 158.07), marking a significant regime shift. While a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage remains, the options market is pricing in downside protection with a strong 25d risk reversal (RR) of -2.20. The negative VRP of -1.3% (IV 7.2% vs HV30 8.5%) suggests that despite the sharp spot move, the options market remains unusually complacent, leaving room for a vol-led spike if the liquidation extends. COT LF net short position of -63,633 remains a significant unwind risk if 158.00 fails to recapture. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; technical break below the SMA cluster targets deeper retracement. Catalyst: US CPI Wednesday. Risk: US 10Y yields rebound sharply above 4.75%, restoring the carry-driven bid.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Outperformance vs Crowded Short
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5894 is holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5836, 0.5790, 0.5829), confirming a bullish technical posture. The pair is supported by a strong positive Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +24.4, the highest in the G10, reflecting a sustained period of data beats. This fundamental strength contrasts sharply with COT positioning, where LF net remains short -30,785 (long% at an extreme 9.7%). This creates an asymmetric short-squeeze setup if upcoming RBNZ signaling remains hawkish, especially as retail sentiment is already 76% short. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; data outperformance targets a squeeze of crowded speculative shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias intact. Risk: RBNZ pivots to a neutral stance, validating the existing short positioning.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Vol Risk Premium + Rate Outlook
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3490, maintaining a position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster centered near 1.3412. The options market is pricing in significant tail-risk with an elevated Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of +4.9% (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.1%), the highest in the G10 space. This suggests traders are paying a heavy premium for protection ahead of Wednesday's US CPI data. While Fed-BoE carry is currently neutral at 0bp, the COT LF net long of +39,039 (70.1% long) indicates that the market is already positioned for GBP resilience. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; elevated vol premium makes new long entries expensive near current levels. Catalyst: US CPI Wednesday. Risk: Sharp drop in US CPI validates Fed hold, driving Cable through 1.3600 on USD weakness.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Sentiment Extreme
signals.text: USD/NOK is currently trading at 9.497, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (9.602, 9.629, 9.706). Retail sentiment has reached a absolute extreme of 100% long, suggesting a complete absence of retail sellers at these levels. This extreme typically serves as a contrarian indicator for a continuation of the downward trend, particularly as the Norges Bank maintains a restrictive real rate of +1.51%. The negative ESI of -6.4 for the USD further supports a weaker USD backdrop. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK; contrarian to 100% retail long positioning. Catalyst: Norges Bank meeting 13 Aug — hike bias priced. Risk: WTI Oil breaks below $75.0, removing the NOK's primary commodity support.
